title: Alibi and Letter
premise: Dominic Sandoval, the cathedral's reclusive archivist, receives two letters in the same hand: one confessing to a murder committed thirty years ago inside the locked crypt, the other promising a second confession if Dominic can find 'the witness who never died.' Following the letters' clues through parish records, Dominic discovers the witness is Elena Voss, the supposed victim's daughter, living under a stolen identity as the cathedral's own bell-ringer. When the crypt is unsealed and the body proves to be someone else entirely, Dominic realizes the confessor is dying and using them to force the truth into daylight before the inheritance that motivated the original crime passes quietly to its architect: the cathedral's beloved dean. In the final confrontation beneath the tower, Elena chooses loyalty over vengeance by testifying truthfully, and Dominic chooses truth over invisibility by signing their own name to the record.
about_author: Casper Nystrom is the pen name of a former parish records clerk from Uppsala who spent a decade cataloguing sealed archives before turning to fiction. They write quiet mysteries about people whose lives are kept in boxes.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Dominic Sandoval, POV. While cataloguing bequests, Dominic receives twin letters postmarked from a hospice: one confessing to a murder in the cathedral's sealed crypt in 1994, the other naming a living witness. The dean dismisses both as a crank's fantasy, but Dominic recognizes the handwriting from old donation ledgers. Emotional beat: unease curdling into compulsion—the first crack in Dominic's carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: The Bell-Ringer Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, with an intercut letter from the dying confessor, Aldous Merrick. Cross-referencing baptismal records, Dominic realizes bell-ringer 'Mara Kell' is Elena Voss, daughter of the murdered man, presumed dead in a fire. When Dominic confronts her, she admits she has been hiding for thirty years—hiding from her uncle, the dean. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two people built on false names.

chapters.title: What the Crypt Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating Dominic and Elena POVs. Forced by Merrick's solicitor, the crypt is opened; the skeleton wears Voss's ring but the teeth belong to the man everyone believed was the killer. The dean moves to have the records sealed and Dominic dismissed, revealing he knows exactly who they both are. Emotional beat: dread and betrayal—the sanctuary itself was the accomplice.

chapters.title: The Second Confession
chapters.summary: Elena's POV closing with Dominic's. At Merrick's deathbed, the full scheme emerges: the dean orchestrated his brother's murder and let Merrick take the guilt, buying silence with the family inheritance now funding the cathedral. Elena must choose between protecting her uncle's legacy and testifying; she speaks, and Dominic signs the sworn statement. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into release—both finally visible, and free.
